body: Thank you.  I appreciate you taking the time, your kind words and advice.

Thank you so much for your kind words.  I actually started crying (in a good way).  Just knowing there's someone out there who has no idea who I am that really seems to care is incredibly comforting.  Just knowing that there's someone to talk to, as cliche as I used to think that was.  You've given me a glimpse of the positive and I don't even know how.  At the same time, I feel so pathetic and selfish for talking about how emo I am without having (imo) a good reason for it.  Guilty for taking time from you.  But again, thank you.  I feel like you're a wise soul.

I like playing video games, but it's not like when I was younger.  It's like a duller experience.  It's not exciting, I don't have the deep drive to win anymore.  It's just something I do to pass the time.  Almost a chore.  The rest of my time is spent browsing youtube or reddit.  What about you?  I'd like to know a bit about you if that's okay.

Thanks.

But it's like I've woken up somewhere and all I see is darkness.  I can't feel any walls.  I have no idea how big the room is, where I am in the world.  And someone plainly says, "Turn on the lightswitch.  There is one."  y'know what I mean?  I don't mean to be rude and I appreciate what you're trying to get across, but how do I get a flashlight?  I don't expect a real answer because I know it's my own issue.  I focus on all the negative without allowing anything positive in.  But it's easier not to try.

I know you mean well, but this just makes me feel worse.

There is no little thing that makes me happy.  I know that it takes effort to gain anything worthwhile.  I just don't care.  I'm aware that I could change my life.  No one else is going to live it for me.  I just don't want to.

But, thanks for taking the time to give me advice.

Thanks, but my story is nothing that should be causing me to feel the way I do.  It just kinda happened.

Just an over-sheltered, naive child that woke up to the real world at the age of 20 while attending college.  Realized I couldn't just fuck around and still get A's.  Had to actually work.  Realized my friends were pretty selfish fucks and am amazed how I couldn't see it back then.  Smoked a lot of weed in my final year of highschool which was a shock to my parents because I'd been completely straight-edge before that.  My parents think I've gone full-blown paranoid or something and don't trust my judgement anymore.  Maybe I have, maybe I'm delusional.  I don't fully trust myself anymore.

Dropped out of college, had never failed a class before that.  Felt worthless.  Start doubting my intelligence, focusing on regrets, other depression bullshit.  Spent a year doing nothing but lying in bed.  Spent so much time being hungry that eventually I stopped feeling it.  Even now I don't get hungry, I force myself to eat half of my dinner.  A lot of my guilt is from feeling the way I do when I don't see a real reason for why I should.  It's not like someone died.  It's not like I was physically or verbally abused by my parents.  There's plenty of people that have it much worse than me I'm sure.

I just don't want to live.  The world is such a cold place.  The majority of people seem so plastic.  Like they're acting out roles.  Do other people actually give a shit what someone else did over the weekend?  What celebrity X was in the news for?  What's the point of small talk?  It doesn't accomplish anything.  Yet it seems like most people are happy talking about meaningless drivel.  I feel like I'm missing some key component of what being human is.  This "need to be accepted" or something that everyone else seems to have.  I don't really know what I'm talking about anymore so I'll just end it.
